text:
Marathon Petroleum edged up 0.35% today as refinery utilization hit 97.4%, near maximum capacity, while U.S. crude held steady around $84 a barrel. High refinery runs and tight inventory levels—particularly low gasoline and diesel stocks—support the economics of converting crude into fuel, which underpins refiner margins and profitability.

The stock's modest gain sits within a volatile two-week pattern marked by geopolitical uncertainty in the Middle East. Ongoing Iran-U.S. tensions and tanker attacks near the Strait of Hormuz (a critical chokepoint for global oil flows) have created both upside risk from supply disruptions and downside risk from de-escalation talks; Europe's historically low gas stores add another layer of supply-demand tightness that could support energy prices, though the outcome remains unclear.
